subject: IR evidence onboarding, brief incident summary and action checklist
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@bluebay-fin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security@bluebay-fin.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: IRP materials + short incident summary

Hi Marissa and Karthik,

We detected a brief authentication anomaly on our integration with Redwood late on 2026-05-03. Our security team has asked for: an executive one-paragraph incident summary, your current Incident Response Plan (IRP) or link to the SOC 2 / SIG sections that cover notification and forensic evidence, and a copy of relevant auth logs for 2026-05-03 (UTC).

We also need a completed IRP questionnaire for our procurement/audit team (attached is our template) and a target timeframe for evidence delivery. This is for our internal tracker (Bridge-Assure audit) and we would like initial materials within 24 hours if possible.

Attachments: customer_ir_request_template.docx (attached to this message)

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Park
Head of Security Operations
BlueBay Financial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@bluebay-fin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: IRP materials + short incident summary

Hi Helen — thanks for the heads up and the template.

Short executive summary (for your tracker):
On 2026-05-03 22:47 UTC our automated anomaly detector flagged a spike in authentication retries from a single client IP associated with BlueBay Financial integrations. The requests resulted in elevated 401 responses but there is no evidence of successful unauthorized access or data exfiltration. Root cause analysis indicates a misconfiguration at the client-side credential rotation process that generated repeated malformed tokens. Redwood mitigations included rate-limiting the source IP, temporary token revocation for the affected client ID, and coordination with the BlueBay engineering team to validate credential rotation behavior. No PII exposure identified.

What we'll deliver and ETA:
- IRP excerpt focussing on notification and evidence handling (SOC 2 / SIG mapping): attached ("irp_questionnaire_v2.pdf") — ETA: immediate (attached)
- Auth logs for 2026-05-03 (UTC): preparing export, will provide CSV of auth events filtered to the BlueBay client ID — ETA: within 6 hours
- Minimal post-incident timeline / draft postmortem: initial draft attached as "postmortem-draft.md" — ETA: EOD tomorrow
- Completed copy of your questionnaire: we will fill and return in the format you attached — ETA: 24 hours

Action items for internal ops (Karthik / Neha): please run the auth export and attach to the thread. Include S3 path and a hash for the file. Also capture any unusual token validation errors from 22:40–23:10 UTC.

We will send a follow-up with the logs and a short forensics note. Please let us know if Bridge-Assure needs additional chain-of-custody or notarization for evidence delivery.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: irp_questionnaire_v2.pdf, postmortem-draft.md
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Helen Park <helen.park@bluebay-fin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: IRP materials + short incident summary

On Mon, May 4, 2026 at 11:05 Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Action items for internal ops (Karthik / Neha): please run the auth export and attach to the thread. Include S3 path and a hash for the file. Also capture any unusual token validation errors from 22:40–23:10 UTC.

Done — I pulled the auth events and filtered to BlueBay client_id=bb_fin_842. Export is uploaded to our secure artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-ops/forensics/20260503/bluebay-auth-export.csv (ACL: restricted). SHA256: d2b4f3a5c89e3f9a2b4a8f6d9c1a0e7b3f4d5c6a7e8f9b0c1d2e3f4b5a6c7d8e.

Notes from logs: repeated token validation failures (malformed JWT signature) starting 2026-05-03T22:45:12Z from IP 198.51.100.42 — average rate ~40 req/min for a 6-minute window. No successful auths observed from that IP after mitigation. No other anomalies in the 22:40–23:10 window.

I attached a CSV stub (auth-logs-20260503.csv) to this thread for quick review. If Bridge-Assure needs raw logs with full headers we can provide a time-limited download link and evidence checklist.

Karthik
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@bluebay-fin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: IRP materials + short incident summary

Thanks Helen / Karthik — appreciate the quick coordination.

Next steps and asks from BlueBay / Bridge-Assure:
- Please confirm receipt of the attached auth CSV and IRP excerpt.
- Let us know if you require a signed chain-of-custody or a DocuSign attestation for the artifact transfer (we can initiate DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/IRP-AUTH-4287).
- We will finalize the postmortem and share a redact-friendly version for your audit team by 2026-05-05 EOD. The internal root cause confirmation is that the client-side credential rotation produced malformed tokens; Redwood's service behaved correctly and applied rate limiting as a protective control.

Attached: postmortem-draft.md (internal draft), irp_questionnaire_v2.pdf, auth-logs-20260503.csv

Marissa Cole
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

P.S. Jonas — once Helen confirms receipt, please add this incident to the quarterly SOC 2 incidents register and mark controls tested for token validation and rate-limiting as in-scope for the 2026 Q2 report.
